spots.notes: Permanent facts only: steep-sided composite cone with a summit caldera in western Haʻapai, connected to Kao by a submarine ridge; Wikivoyage: hire a boat, steep one-hour climb to the crater with views of the crater and Kao, needs serious planning and is expensive (no price given, so cost is the boat hire, not recorded). Wikipedia notes a lava lake as of Aug 2025 (transient; do NOT use in copy). Placement bio says 'crater lake': unverified, drop it. Tourism board lists it as an active volcano. No entry fee found in any source; open island/landscape, no gate or staffed entry. Transport (boat/flight) and local guides are not the price. Treat as unverified: any landing or access fee. Mutiny on the Bounty 1789 nearby is history only.

Sand-cay island in Lifuka district, almost uninhabited, five small resorts and clean quiet beaches (Wikipedia); listed under Tonga Tourism free activities. Default free/open applies; no fee found. Wikivoyage: Fins 'n' Flukes run island trips (transport, not the price). Placement bio claim 'reached on foot at low tide' is unverified; use 'by boat'.

Northernmost island of Tonga, 15 km2, pop 431, volcanic rim island (annular) enclosing crater lakes Vai Lahi and Vai Si'i; erupted regularly since 1814, last major 1985 (history only). Tourism board: hike across craters, swim in freshwater lakes. Pocket Guide: look out for the Tongan megapode. No entry fee found in any source; open island/landscape, no gate or staffed entry. Transport (boat/flight) and local guides are not the price. Placement bio 'reached by air' and 'walked with local guides' unverified here (guide advice is on the Pocket Guide for Niuas generally).

Central crater lake of Niuafo'ou, 'Big Lake', freshwater, 23 m above sea level, four islands (one visible only when the water drops); inner walls forested; locals can take visitors to vantage points. Placement figures '4 km wide and 84 m deep' are NOT in the evidence: unverified, leave out. No entry fee found in any source; open island/landscape, no gate or staffed entry. Transport (boat/flight) and local guides are not the price.

Name means 'sacred island'; volcanic, 16 km2, highest point 157 m, three villages (Hihifo largest in the Niuas), white sandy beaches with lagoons, thatched fales, Hihifo freshwater spring dip, steady steep climb to the high point for views of villages and Tafahi's cone. Wikivoyage: 240 km north of Vava'u, ~1400 people, conservative dress, 2009 tsunami damage (history). No entry fee found in any source; open island/landscape, no gate or staffed entry. Transport (boat/flight) and local guides are not the price. 'Reached by flight from Vava'u' unverified in evidence.

Small island 9 km NNE of Niuatoputapu, closer to Samoa (Savai'i), pop 14, one village; perfectly cone-shaped volcano 656 m, steep climb, Samoa visible on a fine day, guide advised; fishermen cross in outboards almost daily and visitors negotiate a boat ride (price not given; transport is not the spot's cost). Pocket Guide calls it extinct, Wikivoyage 'tiny volcanic satellite island'. 'Reached from Falehau' in placement bio is unverified. No entry fee found in any source; open island/landscape, no gate or staffed entry. Transport (boat/flight) and local guides are not the price.
